title: Étale morphism factorization from the affine limit
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], J a small cofiltered category [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and D : J → X_et a diagram [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] with affine terms [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] open over X [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let c be a limit cone and p : c.pt → X satisfy c_j ≫ D(j).hom = p. For every étale X-object U and q : c.pt → U.left with q ≫ U.hom = p, there exist j and g : D(j).left → U.left with g ≫ U.hom = D(j).hom and c_j ≫ g = q.

proof.text: Form the underlying scheme diagram E and its structure natural transformation to constant X. Affine terms are compact and quasi-separated, and all transition maps are affine.

The étale target is locally of finite presentation. Apply the existing Mathlib factorization theorem to q and the natural-transformation equation obtained from hp and hq. Reorder the two equations in its conclusion.

lean.statement:
theorem affineOpenSections_etale_map_factorization
    {X : Scheme.{u + 1}} {J : Type (u + 1)} [SmallCategory J] [IsCofiltered J]
    (D : J ⥤ X.Etale)
    [∀ j, IsAffine (D.obj j).left] [∀ j, IsOpenImmersion (D.obj j).hom]
    (c : Cone (D ⋙ Scheme.Etale.forget X ⋙ Over.forget X))
    (p : c.pt ⟶ X) (hp : ∀ j, c.π.app j ≫ (D.obj j).hom = p)
    (hc : IsLimit c)
    (U : X.Etale) (q : c.pt ⟶ U.left) (hq : q ≫ U.hom = p) :
    ∃ (j : J) (g : (D.obj j).left ⟶ U.left),
      g ≫ U.hom = (D.obj j).hom ∧ c.π.app j ≫ g = q
